title: KV cache compactness vs fidelity: matrix study for continuous batching
creator: Ayesha Malik
description:
Goal: Measure end-to-end fidelity and runtime benefits for several KV cache compression strategies (per-layer FP8, per-shard INT8, aggressive INT4 packing) within the continuous batching serving path and produce deterministic rollout criteria. Rationale: KV cache is a dominant GPU memory consumer for long-context workloads. Reducing KV memory footprint allows higher batch concurrency and lower p99 latency under bursty load, but compression can change token-level distributions and degrade generation quality. This ticket runs a structured matrix of experiments and produces canary rollouts and monitoring hooks for safe production use.

Scope and deliverables:
- Design and run experiments across 3 axes: numeric format (FP8/INT8/INT4), granularity (layer-wise/shard-wise/global), and fidelity mode (lossy with correction vs lossless packing).
- Measure: token-level divergence (KL/tokens), downstream task delta (perplexity on validation sets, ROUGE/EM on eval tasks), rare-token fidelity metrics, and human-annotated quality for a sampled subset.
- Runtime telemetry: GPU memory footprint, per-request latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), throughput at target SLOs, cache encode/decode CPU overhead, and batching efficiency (tokens/sec/slot).
- Safety & rollout: define acceptance thresholds, automatic fallback to full-precision KV or per-request bypass when divergence exceeds thresholds, and logging for root-cause analysis.
- Artifacts: experiment configs (YAML), scripts for synthetic and real workload replay, evaluation dashboards, and a PR with runtime integration and feature flags.

Experiment matrix summary (examples):
- FP8 per-layer with per-layer scale recalibration and residual correction. Expected: modest memory reduction, minimal fidelity loss on average, good for medium-length contexts.
- INT8 per-shard with bias compensation and online recalibration for hot shards. Expected: large memory wins when many shards are cold; risk of drift for embeddings-heavy prompts.
- INT4 block-packing with stochastic quantization and periodic correction passes. Expected: maximum memory reduction but highest fidelity risk; intended only behind canary and aggressive fallback rules.

Success criteria:
- Quantized variants that reduce KV memory usage by >=30% while keeping perplexity delta <=1.5% and token-level KL below defined thresholds on prod-like workloads.
- No increase in p99 latency >15% under standard load with continuous batching enabled.
- Production rollout plan with automated rollback on fidelity alerts and clear owner for monitoring.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regressions for rare-token/coherent long-range dependencies: mitigate with hybrid scheme (cache low-rank components in higher precision).
- Inconsistent behavior across model architectures: include both decoder-only and encoder-decoder models in the matrix.
- Encoding/decoding CPU overhead negating GPU memory wins: measure CPU/GPU trade-offs and consider moving pack/unpack into GPU kernels where feasible.

Planned timeline:
- Week 1: implement quantized read/write in a staging runtime with feature flags and offline packer.
- Week 2: run matrix sweep on synthetic replay workloads and 3 labeled eval suites.
- Week 3: human evaluation on high-risk prompt cohorts, iterate on correction heuristics.
- Week 4: prepare canary rollout strategy and dashboard; produce PR for runtime-1.22.

Notes: experiment configs will be stored in the repo under experiments/kv-compactness and dashboards in Observability -> KV-Compactness.
